title: Wrexham vs. Portsmouth: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Rich FayNov 27, 2026Wrexham are unbeaten in their previous three home matches. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images (Wrexham), John Walton/PA Images/Getty Images (Portsmouth)Wrexham will hope to give assistant manager Steve Parkin a fitting farewell when they host Portsmouth in the EFL Championship this weekend.

Parkin will step away from soccer at the end of the month to spend more time with his family, bringing an end to an illustrious career and a hugely successful 15-year partnership with Phil Parkinson. The past five of those years have been spent at Wrexham, where he helped take the club from the National League to the Championship, including a club-record finish last season.
The Red Dragons are unbeaten in their previous four matches heading into the weekend, while Portsmouth defeated West Ham United in midweek to continue their strong run of form.

Wrexham lacked creative threat in their midweek draw vs. Bristol City. / Dan Istitene/Getty ImagesWrexham have struggled for goals all season, while Portsmouth boast the best defensive record of any away side in the Championship. It all points toward another tight contest this weekend, which could be decided by a moment of magic or one costly mistake.

The Red Dragons will be desperate to give Parkin the send-off he deserves and could come flying out of the blocks with a point to prove. It won’t be easy against a strong Portsmouth side, though, who have already beaten both West Ham and Swansea City in recent weeks.

Kieffer Moore should return to the lineup after he was rested in midweek. / FotMobWrexham’s lineup will once again be dictated by availability, with no attacking players expected to return to the starting XI this weekend. Parkinson should name an unchanged defensive lineup given how much stronger the team has looked in recent weeks.
He could bring Ben Sheaf or Matty James into midfield to provide more control, although the wingbacks should remain unchanged, with Lewis O’Brien likely to play behind Kieffer Moore in attack.
Wrexham predicted lineup (3-5-1-1): Patterson; Cleworth, Worrall, Doyle; Kaboré, Whiteman, Sheaf, Thomason, Ekomié; O'Brien; Moore.

Portsmouth could refresh their attack in North Wales. / FotMob.Portsmouth have an injury crisis of their own, with just 20 senior players expected to be available for their trip to North Wales and 10 players still sidelined.
John Mousinho’s side should also name an unchanged backline against Wrexham, although they could make changes in attack, with Josh Murphy potentially returning and Tyrese Shade leading the line.
Portsmouth predicted lineup (4-2-3-1): Schmid; Devlin, Poole, Dia, Swanson; Pack, Mohamed; Kavuma-McQueen, Bailey, Murphy; Shade.
